# Change record: 2026-10-17-round-13-review-readability

*Generated by `spec` from the YAML file beside it. Don't edit this file by hand.*

*2026-10-17 · code-first · target: python · closed 2026-10-17*

**Request (summarized):** Make the review surfaces readable without looking anything up (SYS-30): proposals show each item's full text and context, every ID in a generated view links to its item with its text on hover, and the approval reader understands IDs written like 'Change 13'

## Open decisions, most consequential first

- **D1: Which of an agent's decision records should be proposed for your explicit approval?**
  - *Why it ranks here:* It decides how many decision records land in front of you each round. Right now AGENT-51 proposes every record that weighed alternatives, which is nearly all of them, and that's how DR-45, DR-47 and DR-48 reached you in round 12.
  - *Involves:* AGENT-51 (The agent shall propose for explicit approval each item…)
  - ⚠ *Read before accepting; these carry your words or recorded decisions:* AGENT-51 (your words)
  1. Only those whose consequences reach you **(recommended)**: Propose an agent's decision record only when it changes what you see, approve or do: DR-47 (approving a need delegates what's under it) qualifies, DR-45 (how approval history is stored) doesn't. The rest stay recorded and delegated: future agents read them as reasoning and may revise them, recording why.
  2. Every record that weighed alternatives: Today's rule. Nothing slips past you, at the cost of reading mechanics like DR-45 and DR-48.
  3. Never: Agent decision records stay as memory only. Choices that matter to you would have to surface as requirements or open decisions instead.

To accept every recommendation: `.syseng/spec resolve D1 --words "<your words>"`.

- **add DR-49 (Review sections carry their context inline instead of linking…)**: design decision of round 13.
  - title: Review sections carry their context inline instead of linking to it

  - consequences: Change records get longer, and the same text can appear in two sections. Each review section can be read on its own.
- **modify DR-41 (Chat approvals are recorded only when they name items…)**: the engineer's "Change 13 LGTM." would have been read as approving nothing.
  - decision, before: ~~The prompt hook reads each line of the engineer's message on its own. A line approves when it starts with "approve" (or "approved") and its first clause names only item IDs and ranges, or when it is only item IDs followed by "LGTM", "approved" or "looks good", as in "SYS-32 LGTM". - It records the whole message as the engineer's words, marked as given in chat, and tells the agent what it recorded. - Any other approval, such as "approve everything except the wording ones", records nothing. The hook tells the agent to show the exact list, leaving out every item an exception could refer to, and to get the engineer's confirmation, in a menu where the harness has one. - Quoted lines and pasted text never count, and a capitalized word counts as a system element only when that element exists. A message with "lgtm" or "looks good" and no IDs gets a note that it approves nothing.~~
  - decision, now:
    The prompt hook reads each line of the engineer's message on its own. A line approves when it starts with "approve" (or "approved") and its first clause names only item IDs and ranges, or when it is only item IDs followed by "LGTM", "approved" or "looks good", as in "SYS-32 LGTM".
    - An ID may be written as a word and a number, such as "Change 13", when the word names a system element, needs or decision records (AGENT-57).
    - It records the whole message as the engineer's words, marked as given in chat, and tells the agent what it recorded.
    - Any other approval, such as "approve everything except the wording ones", records nothing. The hook tells the agent to show the exact list, leaving out every item an exception could refer to, and to get the engineer's confirmation, in a menu where the harness has one.
    - Quoted lines and pasted text never count, and a capitalized word counts as a system element only when that element exists. A message with "lgtm" or "looks good" and no IDs gets a note that it approves nothing.
